messages:
sophia: Heads up — planning an interconnect firmware swap in az4 that will require rolling node drains for the saturn GPU pool. Target window Tue 02:00-05:00 UTC. Primary risk is brief egress oscillation when we move cohorts.

ken: Thanks — can you scope which cohorts/nodes? We should avoid draining any cohort that currently hosts long KV-seeded sessions.

sophia: We'll do cohort rotation by rack: cohort-3 then cohort-1 then cohort-4. Each cohort = ~24 nodes, drain duration ~10-12m, 5m cooldown. Plan: drain -> reboot NIC -> verify egress stats -> uncordon.

maria: FYI EU customers have a scheduled job around 02:30 UTC that hits saturn heavily. Can we shift that job or move it to a fallback pool?

sophia: Good catch. Ops will reach out to the job owner. If not possible, we can reorder racks to avoid the busiest tenant during their window.

infra-bot: calendar: "az4 interconnect firmware swap" created for Tue 02:00-05:00 UTC. Incident channel #eng-infra will be notified 30m prior.

alex: What fallback do we expect? We have reserved capacity in eu-west that can take non-latency-sensitive work, but cross-region egress costs will apply. Estimate ~0.4c/token additional for heavy jobs.

priyanka: Cost mitigation idea: route embeddings-heavy jobs to the cached embedding cluster (omega) temporarily and throttle low-priority generation traffic. Also enable kv-cache pre-seeding on the backfill nodes to reduce token spend.

ken: How will this affect Dedicated tenants? Do we have SLA exposures?

sophia: Dedicated pools pinned to az4 are impacted if customers are on saturn cohort racks. For those we have two options: (1) brief capacity handoff to cross-az dedicated reserve (small percentage) or (2) defer maintenance for high-SLA tenants and do a hotpatch limited to control plane only. We should surface tradeoffs to account and PMs.

maria: Suggest we publish a short customer comms draft — keep it simple: expected <3% capacity reduction per minute, transient latency bump for bursty jobs, no data loss.

sophia: Draft I plan to send: "Planned maintenance Tue 02:00-05:00 UTC in az4 affecting a subset of GPU capacity. Expect short rolling drains with brief latency increases; jobs will either fallback or queue. Contact support if you need to request an exempt window." Thoughts?

oncall: +1 on comms. Also request that oncall gets a preflight checklist in thread: health checks, canary job, rollback command.

ken: Preflight checklist (short):
- confirm canary job (small batch embed) passes
- KV cache seed on backfill nodes
- `fleetctl drain --pool=saturn --cohort=cohort-3 --reason=interconnect-fw` ready
- smoke-check: top-10-tenant-latency < 200ms before uncordon
- rollback: `fleetctl uncordon --force` and pin traffic to reserved pool

priyanka: We'll prepare routing rules for low-priority throttling and enable spot fallback for burst capacity. Ops: estimate incremental cost if full cohort reroutes to eu-west for 30m?

alex: Rough calc: cohort 24 nodes handling ~1.2M tokens/min at peak. If rerouted to cross-region paid capacity, ballpark $300-450 for 30m if they hit peak. If we throttle to 50% it's ~150-225.

maria: Ok — include cost estimate in comms for internal stakeholders only. Customers get an abstracted message.

sophia: Ops will own sequencing. I'll open a pager for Tue 01:30 UTC to run preflight. Can everyone ack readiness by EOD?

ken: Ack. I'll prep the drain/un-drain playbook and post it to the runbook repo.

priyanka: Ack — routing + throttle rules in place, will QA today.

alex: Ack, will notify finance for potential cost cover.

maria: Ack, reaching out to the EU job owner to request quiet window.

infra-bot: reminder: oncall @channel in 30 minutes before scheduled maintenance.

sophia: Thanks all. If anything blocks, call me on the escalation channel. :thumbsup:
